summary: Thirteen experiments completed in 11.4 minutes, including seven compute-bound experiments. The 8.73-minute SOTA constraint-saturation and bounded-intervention comparison dominated the recorded execution tail, but the bounded data has no phase breakdown and the locked record reports no GPU-idle condition on compute-bound tasks.
bottlenecks_identified: The 8.73-minute SOTA constraint-saturation and bounded-intervention comparison dominated the 11.4-minute milestone wall time.
Disk-mtime reconstruction provides no per-phase timing, so the data does not reveal why the longest compute-bound experiment took longest.
The GPU report is not attributed to task execution windows, so it cannot establish accelerator duty cycle during the seven compute-bound experiments.
improvements_suggested: Add monotonic per-phase timing and task-correlated GPU utilization receipts to every compute-bound run.
Declare model count at dispatch and record the selected runner; invoke DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded in parallel.
Add dependency-aware scheduling that can overlap synthesis-only work with compute-bound work when prerequisites permit, and record the achieved overlap.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument the 8.73-minute compute tail with phase timers and task-linked GPU samples.
Add model-count and runner-selection receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel multi-model tasks.
Measure and enable safe overlap between synthesis-only and compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The supplied record can rank durations but cannot explain phase causality or grade task-window GPU efficiency. No data available this milestone establishes a compute-bound task with at least two models in parallel or a failure to engage DualGPURunner.
